newsitem.title: INDIA: India customs/excise revenue below target Q1 97/98.
newsitem.headline: India customs/excise revenue below target Q1 97/98.

text.p: India's revenue collection from excise and customs duties in the first quarter of the current fiscal year 1997/98 (April-March) is below target, a senior finance ministry official said on Monday.
"In the first quarter collections are below target," R. Gopalnathan, chairman of Central Board of Excise and Customs told reporters. He did not give figures for the first quarter revenue collected.

India hopes to gather 522 billion rupees ($14.58 billion) from excise and 525.50 billion rupees from customs duties in 1997/98. In the last fiscal year the government received 461.90 billion rupees from excise and 441.35 billion rupees from custom duties.
"We are confident of meeting the excise revenue targets," said Gopalnathan. "In customs, certain things like exchange rate, imports are beyond our control."
Industrial output grew by only 6.7 percent in 1996/97 compared with 11.6 percent in the previous year.

The output of domestic industry is expected to grow by at least 11 percent in the current fiscal year, Press Trust of India news agency quoted a senior industry ministry official as saying earlier on Monday.
Indian merchandise exports fell to $5.40 billion in April and May, down 1.98 percent from $5.51 billion in the same two-month period in 1996.
Imports declined by 0.6 percent to $6.24 billion in first two months of the current fiscal year from $6.28 billion in the same period last year.
Gopalnathan said the government would streamline tax administration and improve compliance to yield better revenue collection. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
